title: Can metal-on-metal hip implants cause local or systemic effects?

grade.title: Small, uncontrolled, or single-source human evidence
grade.basis: One scientific committee opinion describes local reactions and says systemic organ toxicity is not established.

answerHtml: SCENIHR said metal-on-metal implants may cause local and systemic adverse effects. Local responses range from small asymptomatic lesions to severe bone and soft-tissue destruction. Large-diameter implants had the highest incidence of local reactions. Evidence for systemic organ toxicity, carcinogenicity, and teratogenicity was judged insufficient.

sections.heading: Opinion
sections.html: Terms used in the opinion include metallosis, ALVAL, pseudotumours, and ARMD. Whole-blood cobalt screening and the 2 to 7 µg/L range are on the cobalt and ion-test pages. SCENIHR PDF. A later SCHEER opinion on these hips was not located.

sources.text: SCENIHR opinion on metal-on-metal joint replacements, 2014

buyHtml:

The program states that certification is a measurement of a product against a published limit, not a statement that the product is safe. If a licensee is later listed for this category, it will be on the register.
